summary:
CropLite is a web-based agricultural decision-support platform that helps farmers make informed planting decisions using NASA Earth observation data and historical climate information.

Developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, CropLite addresses the challenge of adapting agricultural practices to increasingly variable environmental conditions.

Users can select their farmland on an interactive satellite map and explore local environmental conditions, including temperature, precipitation, solar radiation, and atmospheric humidity.

By combining NASA POWER climate data, Copernicus satellite observations, and crop-specific agronomic parameters, CropLite evaluates the suitability of ten agricultural crops. Its recommendation engine considers thermal requirements, growing degree days, and estimated water availability to identify promising cultivation alternatives.

The platform also proposes annual crop rotation sequences, considering growing seasons, crop compatibility, and planting schedules.

CropLite transforms complex environmental datasets into accessible, understandable agricultural insights, helping users explore more sustainable farming strategies while clearly communicating the limitations and uncertainties of its recommendations.
details:
The Problem

Agriculture is increasingly affected by climate variability, changing precipitation patterns, and environmental uncertainty. Farmers must decide which crops to plant and when to plant them, often without easy access to the scientific information needed to evaluate their options.

Although satellites and environmental monitoring systems generate enormous amounts of valuable data, translating that information into practical agricultural decisions remains challenging.

Our Solution

CropLite is an interactive agricultural planning platform designed to bridge the gap between Earth observation data and everyday farming decisions.

Our goal is to make scientifically informed agricultural planning more accessible, understandable, and practical.

Users begin by selecting their agricultural land on an interactive satellite map. CropLite then retrieves environmental information relevant to the selected location and transforms it into meaningful indicators.

The platform offers three core capabilities:

Environmental monitoring

CropLite integrates historical information from NASA POWER and satellite observations from Copernicus Sentinel-2.

Users can explore variables such as temperature, precipitation, solar radiation, atmospheric humidity, evapotranspiration, and vegetation indices.

These indicators help users understand the environmental characteristics of their selected area.

Intelligent crop recommendations

CropLite evaluates ten agricultural crops using a transparent, rule-based agronomic recommendation engine.

The system examines several factors, including:

  • Temperature suitability and thermal exposure.
  • Growing degree days (GDD).
  • Historical climatic variability.
  • Precipitation and estimated crop water requirements.
  • Crop-specific growing cycles and phenological characteristics.

Rather than simply presenting environmental measurements, CropLite interprets them to identify potentially suitable crops and communicate the reasoning behind its recommendations.

The platform distinguishes historical observations from estimates and assumptions. Its suitability scores represent comparative assessments, not guaranteed yields or predictions of agricultural success.

Annual crop rotation planning

CropLite generates potential crop sequences within a single agricultural year.

Its planning engine considers crop duration, planting and harvesting windows, seasonal compatibility, and botanical family diversity.

The objective is to help users explore alternative planting strategies while reducing scheduling conflicts and encouraging more diversified agricultural practices.

The resulting plans are preliminary recommendations and do not replace local knowledge of soil fertility, irrigation, or crop management.

Technology and Development

CropLite was developed using a modern web architecture:

Frontend: React, JavaScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Leaflet for the interactive user interface and geographic visualization.

Backend: Python and FastAPI for environmental data processing, agronomic calculations, and recommendation generation.

Environmental data sources:

  • NASA POWER for historical agroclimatic information.
  • Copernicus Sentinel-2 for vegetation monitoring through satellite-derived indicators such as NDVI.
  • Esri World Imagery for geographic satellite visualization.
  • FAO agronomic references for crop requirements and cultivation parameters.

CropLite combines these technologies into a unified platform that transforms scientific datasets into visual, understandable information.

Innovation and Creativity

CropLite's innovation lies in combining several layers of agricultural intelligence within one accessible application.

Instead of requiring users to interpret satellite datasets, climate tables, and agronomic references separately, CropLite brings these sources together into an integrated decision-making experience.

The platform connects geographic field selection, historical environmental analysis, crop evaluation, and annual planting strategies.

Its recommendation engine emphasizes transparency and explainability, allowing users to understand the environmental factors influencing each assessment.

The interface was designed to communicate complex scientific information through intuitive maps, visual indicators, and clear comparisons.

Expected Impact

CropLite aims to make data-informed agricultural planning more accessible, especially to small and medium-sized farmers who may not have access to specialized agricultural analysis tools.

By improving access to environmental information, the project could support better-informed planting decisions, encourage crop diversification, and help farmers investigate adaptation strategies under changing climatic conditions.

CropLite also demonstrates how NASA's openly accessible Earth science data can be transformed into practical digital tools that connect scientific research with real-world agricultural challenges.

Our vision is simple: Plan smarter. Grow better.
